key_insight: The paper reframes visual generation from appearance synthesis to "intelligent visual generation" via a five-level taxonomy (from atomic mapping to agentic world modeling), emphasizing structure, dynamics, and causal grounding for plausibility and long-horizon consistency.
problem_solved: Addresses limitations of current visual generation models—poor spatial reasoning, lack of persistent state, weak long-horizon consistency, and limited causal understanding—by providing a conceptual roadmap to build models that generate visuals grounded in world structure and dynamics.
method: Introduce a five-level taxonomy spanning atomic mapping → compositional/structured representations → dynamic simulation → agentic world modeling to classify capability stages and gaps.
Analyze existing visual generation models against the taxonomy to pinpoint common failure modes (spatial errors, state drift, causal brittleness).
Propose research directions and evaluation priorities (structured state representations, learned dynamics, causal modules, interactive/agentic components) to advance toward agentic world models.
impact: Gives AI/ML practitioners a compact framework to prioritize model design and benchmarks for next‑generation visual systems that reason, maintain state, and support interactive applications—relevant for AR, robotics, simulation, and creative tools.
visual_elements: A 5-level vertical taxonomy diagram (label each level from atomic mapping to agentic world modeling) with brief capability examples per level.
Capability gap chart comparing current SOTA features (photorealism, typography, instruction following) vs. missing abilities (spatial reasoning, persistent state, causal inference).
Before/after sequence panels showing a model failing vs. succeeding at long‑horizon consistency or object permanence.
Architecture sketch of an agentic world model: perception → structured state → dynamics/physics module → planner/agent → renderer.
paper_title: Visual Generation in the New Era: An Evolution from Atomic Mapping to Agentic World Modeling
paper_authors: Keming Wu, Zuhao Yang, Kaichen Zhang, Shizun Wang, Haowei Zhu
